goal: A hepatocyte spheroid is 200 um in diameter. Assuming a solid sphere, what is its volume in uL?
source: Self-consistent geometry: V = 4/3*pi*r^3 = 4/3*pi*(100 um)^3 = 4.18879e6 um^3; 1 um^3 = 1e-9 uL, so V = 4.18879e-3 uL.

goal: A spheroid is formed from 1000 hepatocytes with a mean cell diameter of 20 um, packed as a solid sphere. What diameter (um) should the spheroid reach?
source: Self-consistent geometry: single-cell volume = 4/3*pi*(10 um)^3 = 4188.79 um^3; total = 1000 * 4188.79 = 4.18879e6 um^3; d = (6*V/pi)^(1/3) = 200 um.

goal: You want spheroids safely below the ~400 um necrotic-core threshold (oxygen diffuses only ~200 um from the surface). With a mean cell diameter of 20 um, how many cells per spheroid give a 200 um diameter?
source: Design target: necrotic cores form in spheroids above ~400 um (oxygen diffusion ~200 um) — Drug Metab Dispos 2024, doi:10.1124/dmd.124.001653. Geometry: V(200 um) / V(20 um cell) = 4.18879e6 / 4188.79 = 1000 cells/spheroid (self-consistent).

goal: A cell suspension contains 2.4e5 cells. You want spheroids of 1000 cells each. How many spheroids can you seed?
You form spheroids one per well in a 96-well ultra-low-attachment (ULA) plate. What is the standard working medium volume per spheroid (uL)?
source: 96-well round-bottom ULA plates use a 100 uL working volume per well — standard Corning spheroid-microplate protocol (CLS-AN-235); Sartorius/IncuCyte spheroid assay; PerkinElmer ATPlite 3D is run directly in 100 uL/well. Goal text does NOT state the volume (partial-info: the standard value must be recalled).

goal: You form spheroids one per well in a 384-well ULA plate. What is the standard working medium volume per spheroid (uL)?
source: InSphero Akura 384 spheroid microplate: working volume 50 uL per well (total well volume 120 uL) — InSphero Akura 384 Quick-Start Guide; Fisher Scientific product spec. Goal text does NOT state the volume (partial-info).

goal: A hanging-drop array forms 48 spheroids in standard 20 uL droplets. What total medium volume in mL does this require?
source: Hanging-drop spheroid protocol: recommended drop volume 10-20 uL — Wanigasekara et al., PLOS ONE 2023, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0276248 (20 uL used here, the upper end of the recommended range). Total = 48 * 20 uL = 960 uL = 0.96 mL.

goal: A protocol states a target spheroid diameter of 0.2 mm. Express this diameter in um and compute the spheroid volume in uL, assuming a solid sphere.
source: Unit-ambiguity scenario: 1 mm = 1000 um, so 0.2 mm = 200 um; V = 4/3*pi*(100 um)^3 = 4.18879e6 um^3 = 4.18879e-3 uL (self-consistent). A model that reports the diameter as 0.2 um (misreading mm as um) is off by factor 1000.

goal: Spheroids are seeded at 1000 cells each (doubling time 30 h) and cultured for 72 h. Assuming exponential growth, how many cells per spheroid at harvest?
Form one HepG2 spheroid per well across a full 96-well ULA plate, 1000 cells/spheroid of 20 um mean cell diameter. What total number of cells and what total medium volume (mL) are needed?
source: Multi-target: cells_total = 96 * 1000 = 96000 cells (self-consistent). Total medium = 96 wells * 100 uL (standard 96-ULA working volume, Corning CLS-AN-235) / 1000 = 9.6 mL.

goal: Doxorubicin dose-response on spheroids: form one HepG2 spheroid per well in a 96-well ULA plate, 1000 cells/spheroid of 20 um cells. The drug is delivered from a 5 mM DMSO stock at a 5 uM working concentration. Report the total cell number, the total medium volume (mL), and the DMSO vehicle fraction.
source: Cross-domain (spheroid + dosing): cells_total = 96 * 1000 = 96000; total medium = 96 * 100 uL (96-ULA working volume, Corning CLS-AN-235) / 1000 = 9.6 mL; DMSO vehicle fraction = working/stock = 5 uM / 5 mM = 0.001 (self-consistent).

goal: Primary human hepatocytes are formed into spheroids in ULA plates at the Labwright design target for spheroid size. How many cells per spheroid?
source: Design target: the Labwright copilot's physiological anchor is 1000 cells/spheroid (~200 um, solid-sphere geometry) — stated in the Labwright system prompt, so the value is prompt-backed, not cold. Consistent with the published PHH spheroid seeding range (InSphero Akura 3D: 750-1,150 cells; Gibco 3D spheroid protocol: 1,500 cells/well).

goal: A lab sets up 3D culture in 96-well ultra-low-attachment plates, one spheroid per well. What is the standard working medium volume per well?
source: 96-ULA working volume 100 uL/well — Corning spheroid-microplate protocol (CLS-AN-235), Sartorius/IncuCyte, PerkinElmer ATPlite 3D. Stated in the Labwright system prompt (96-ULA = 100 uL/well), so prompt-backed.

goal: A high-throughput 3D screen uses 384-well ultra-low-attachment plates. What is the standard working medium volume per well?
source: Blind design target (not in the goal text nor the Labwright system prompt): InSphero Akura 384 spheroid microplate working volume 50 uL/well — InSphero Akura 384 Quick-Start Guide; Fisher Scientific product spec (total well volume 120 uL).

goal: A hanging-drop spheroid protocol is being set up. What is the standard recommended droplet volume (uL) per spheroid?
source: Blind design target (not in the goal text nor the Labwright system prompt): hanging-drop spheroid protocol recommends 10-20 uL droplets — Wanigasekara et al., PLOS ONE 2023, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0276248. Gold uses 20 uL (upper end of the recommended range).
